[Section] Analysis ::: Impact of initialization
[source_id=57] Initializing foreign embeddings is the backbone of our approach. A good initialization leads to better zero-shot transfer results and enables fast adaptation. To verify the importance of a good initialization, we train a RAMEN$_{\textsc {base}}$+RoBERTa with foreign word-embeddings are initialized randomly from $\mathcal {N}(0, {1}{d^2})$. For a fair comparison, we use the same hyper-parameters in §SECREF27. Table TABREF36 shows the results of XNLI and UD parsing of random initialization. In comparison to the initialization using aligned fastText vectors, random initialization decreases the zero-shot performance of RAMEN$_{\textsc {base}}$ by 15.9% for XNLI and 27.8 points for UD parsing on average. We also see that zero-shot parsing of SOV languages (Arabic and Hindi) suffers random initialization.
